NestJS is not mentioned anywhere despite being a top-weighted must_mirror item -- candidate lists Node.js/Express-adjacent stacks (Spring Boot, FastAPI, Next.js) but no NestJS, which will be an instant gap in phone screen if interviewer probes framework specifics. HTML/CSS are absent from skills section entirely -- easy fix, add them even if implicit in frontend work. On plausibility: the co-op timeline at Dassault (June 2025-Jan 2026) is only ~7 months long yet claims ownership of a full recommendation system with two-tower embeddings, a Redis caching layer, Hibernate tuning, 99% test coverage across microservices, AND a WebSocket/GraphQL virtual companion module -- that's 4 substantial owned initiatives for a co-op in under 8 months, which reads as scope-inflation and will not survive 'walk me through how you built the two-tower embedding model' questioning. The LSEG bullet claiming solo build of Kafka-Elasticsearch pipelines processing 1.4B daily records for a 4-person team, while simultaneously citing joint ownership with two backend engineers in the bullet above, is an internal inconsistency in team size/ownership that a screener will flag -- clarify team boundaries per bullet. 'Cut SQL-based databases latency 70%' is awkward mirrored phrasing that reads as keyword-stuffing rather than a natural claim -- rewrite as 'Cut database query latency 70% via Redis caching and Hibernate tuning on SQL-based (PostgreSQL) systems' to keep the keyword but sound engineer-authored. No mention of Scrum/Kanban explicitly (only 'Agile/Scrum sprint ceremonies' buried in a bullet) -- surface it in skills. Overall stack breadth (Java, Python, TS, Angular, Next.js, LangChain, Terraform) across 2.5 years of experience is very wide; interviewer will likely drill into 2-3 claims only, so candidate must be ready to defend Redis+Hibernate tuning and Kafka+ES pipeline specifics in detail since those are the most checkable claims.

Team-scoping is the main red flag: original source says 'Developed a...POC' (implying solo/small effort) but rendered resume adds 'as a co-op engineer' framing that's fine, though the '4-person team' and 'jointly with two backend engineers' at LSEG are new specifics not in source_evidence — these should be verifiable in interview since they add precision not present in ground truth. The 'Cut SQL-based databases latency 70%' bullet directly mirrors JD's 'SQL-based databases' keyword — plausible since Hibernate/Redis work supports it, but interviewer will probe exact DB engine (Postgres vs MSSQL vs Oracle) which resume never specifies. TDD/JUnit claim in bullet 2 is plausible given regression suite work but candidate should be ready to describe actual TDD workflow (test-first) vs. just using JUnit for regression, as these are technically distinct practices. No NestJS or TypeScript backend experience is evidenced anywhere in source (TypeScript only listed as skill, not demonstrated in bullets) — this is the biggest plausibility gap against the JD's top-weighted 'NestJS' and 'Typescript' requirements; recommend not implying backend TS/NestJS depth beyond what's listed in skills section, since no bullet demonstrates it and a technical screen will expose this. 'Service oriented systems' and 'financial systems' are well-supported by LSEG bullets. Overall claims are aggressive but mostly traceable to source evidence; the main exposure is on TypeScript/NestJS specificity and the added team-size details.
